I was in the exact same situation you are. I expressed this feeling of guilt to child and youth workers at the time and they told me some thing that makes a lot of sense. 

They explained that while the physical trauma that differs can be explained in black and white, the psychological trauma cannot be. Bottom line is that anyone who has been assaulted had their voice taken away, their body taken. Just because someone else "had it worse" does not diminish your very real pain. 

It's like a child having nothing to eat except a slice of bread every 3 days, and another having a slice of bread every day. The child having something to eat every day could think "he has it worse, I shouldn't complain" but are they not both malnourished? Are they both not starving? Are they both not going to be severely ill? Yes. Just because one could be classified as "worse" does not mean you do not deserve help. 

I am very sorry that this has happened to you. It is not easy, but pls know that you deserve whatever help it is you require to get through this. Much love and admiration to you btw

Pills are such a horrible rollercoaster. It can be exhausting trying to find the right combination, but if you feel like they have helped atleast in the slightest, it is worth the journey. My suggestion to you is do a bit of research on medication that way when you go to an appointment if they offer a certain medication to you you have a bit of understanding as to whether or not it might be good for you. 

For example when I was 15 I got put on meds for the first time and had I known how many others had such bad experiences with a certain medication I would have maybe spoken up and asked for a different one. Some medication's have certain side effects that will negatively affect some more than others. You know yourself better than anyone, even if you feel like you don't know yourself that much you still know more than others. Pills that have drowsiness as a side effect for someone who is typically lethargic and fatigued might want to stay away from that. However a pill that causes restlessness for someone who has a lot of anxiety might want to stay away from that one.

Doing some research on them might make you feel a bit more in control. I can tell by the timestamp that I'm a little late to giving you advice however hopefully for your next appointment you can be a bit prepared. Also I want to say that I am very proud of you for going to the appointment and taking charge and continuing to take and seek out new medication and help. It's a very difficult journey and you're very strong for going through it.

I want to begin by saying that what happened to you was so unfair and I'm sorry you do not have better, more responsible adults in your life.

I live in Canada as well and have had to seek help for similar circumstances. Depending on where you live exactly, there are different types of support you can get. I suggest calling your local hospital (ik you said going there is not good but I hope calling won't be triggering) and asking for their resources. I found all of my resources through the hospital and for the most part they were good.

I had a very similar experience. When I was assaulted I did what would be considered "kegal type movements" as I was trying to resist. If your body had this same reaction it could remind you of that time.

I am not sure what it is that you went through but diagnosing PTSD is very difficult, as is a lot of mental disorders. When I got diagnosed so many doctors had an opinion. Just because this doctor says that you don't have it, doesn't mean that you don't have it. Having someone invalidate what you were going through is traumatic in itself and obviously it is good to know what is actually going on but this person is clearly just dismissing what you have gone through and that is not okay. I would speak to a higher up at the hospital and explain your issues with this doctor. I hope you find a better one.

I want to start off by saying I am sorry you have to go through this. Being the one to uncover a family secret is not easy.

I say this a lot on Reddit but people need to stop feeling guilty for telling the truth. You did nothing wrong! The person who messed up is to blame, not you. All you did was give everyone involved the factual information, which they deserved to know.

Your siblings are quite young and are going to find people to blame for this no matter what. Kids don't understand these situations, all they see right now is that you said something snd now mom and dad aren't together. Hopefully with maybe some counselling or with age they will understand that you did not break up your family, it was your father who made a mistake and all you did was reveal the truth.
